core.title: Keep Acceptance and DESIRED OUTCOME bindings out of journey specs
core.given: A journey spec: a test file that the stack's role assignment does not exclude from journey-spec candidacy, and that either (a) is recognized by the stack's e2e-test naming AND is of an e2e-test kind (both conditions are required on this naming branch), or (b) carries a user/system flow or journey binding in its header comments, whatever its name. Test files that the stack's role assignment excludes from journey-spec candidacy are never journey specs, even when they carry journey bindings.
core.when: the spec is written or edited
core.then: The journey spec MUST NOT carry the acceptance or DESIRED OUTCOME header binding lines.
prefer: Move acceptance assertions out of the journey spec into an acceptance test that declares the Acceptance/DESIRED_OUTCOME pair.
Or simply drop the acceptance/DESIRED_OUTCOME binding lines and keep the spec bound only to its user/system flow or journey.
avoid: Giving one test both a journey identity (user-system-flow/journey) and an acceptance identity (Acceptance/DESIRED_OUTCOME).
Renaming a journey spec away from the stack's e2e-test naming to escape the check while it keeps a journey binding — misnamed specs are still judged.
Treating a test file that the stack's role assignment excludes from journey-spec candidacy as a journey spec.
unless: Vendored and generated trees are never scanned (the stack's excluded roots).
core.why: Journey and acceptance identities are exclusive: a journey test binds to a user/system flow or journey, an acceptance test to an Acceptance/DESIRED_OUTCOME pair. Carrying both makes the test ambiguous about what it proves.
evidence: The journey-spec header scan reports no journey spec whose header comments contain the acceptance or DESIRED OUTCOME binding lines.

Either fix is valid: the acceptance/DESIRED_OUTCOME lines were dropped from the journey spec, or — if acceptance assertions were moved — they appear in an acceptance test carrying the Acceptance/DESIRED_OUTCOME pair.
verification: A header-comment scan over test files. A file is a journey spec when it is not excluded from journey-spec candidacy by the stack's role assignment and either (a) matches the stack's e2e-test naming AND is of an e2e-test kind — naming alone is not enough — or (b) its header comment lines carry a user/system flow or journey binding, so a misnamed spec is still judged.
The scan matches header comment binding lines only, not string literals — a test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string literal is not flagged.

Test files that the stack's role assignment excludes from journey-spec candidacy are excluded unconditionally, even when they carry journey bindings. Which files (if any) are excluded is stack data from the profile's role assignment; a stack that excludes none simply has no such files. Classifying a test file's kind needs a classifier.
Vendored and generated trees are never scanned; the exact exclusion is the stack-wide excluded-roots list owned by the checker.
Disposition: strict — a finding blocks the check run rather than merely warning; severity 3. Severity and disposition are per-rule enforcement facts held with the rule, not profile keys.

fires: A test file of an e2e-test kind, recognized by the stack's e2e-test naming, carries the acceptance binding line.

A test file of an e2e-test kind not named as an e2e test, and not excluded from journey-spec candidacy, whose header carries a journey or user/system flow binding also carries the DESIRED OUTCOME binding.
An agent adds acceptance/DESIRED_OUTCOME binding lines to an existing journey spec to link it to an acceptance.
doesNotFire: A test file excluded from journey-spec candidacy by the stack's role assignment, carrying the acceptance and DESIRED OUTCOME bindings, with or without a journey marker — it is never a journey spec.
A test file excluded from journey-spec candidacy by the stack's role assignment whose header carries a journey binding together with acceptance/DESIRED_OUTCOME binding lines.
A test that merely mentions a journey URN inside a string literal.
Files under the stack's vendored and generated (excluded) trees.

bunOnly.reason: The specific excluded runner (bun test) is a Bun realization fact; the core states the exclusion generically via the profile's role assignment without assuming every stack separates runners.

bunOnly.text: A bun test file is never a journey spec — exclude bun test files unconditionally, even if they carry journey markers.
bunOnly.reason: Runner-specific exclusion of the Bun stack; the core keeps the unconditional-exclusion mechanism generic (roles.assignment) and does not tie it to the stack's test-runner key.

neutralityNotes: User/system flow, journey, Acceptance and DESIRED OUTCOME are ATDD artifact concepts (urn parameters), not stack names. The naming branch now requires both the profiled e2e naming (suffix.e2e_test) and an e2e-test kind (roles.e2e_test.kinds; Playwright in Bun), matching bun.json. tooling.test_runner is no longer used: the unconditional exclusion of bun test files is expressed generically as files that the profile's role assignment (roles.assignment) excludes from journey-spec candidacy, which a single-runner stack may leave empty, and the concrete bun-test exclusion is also kept explicitly in bunOnly (avoid[2], verifier_detail[2]). The detector id and policy.strict-disposition reference are realization details in bunOnly; core:verification carries severity 3 and strict disposition generically.
